test_title: SSC Stenographer 2025 Official Paper (Held On: 08 Aug, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
Match the following cave sites with their architectural characteristics:

 
 

 
 
**Column A-Cave Site **

 
 
 
**Column B-Architectural Feature**

 
 
 

 
 
A.

 
 Udayagiri
 
 
1.

 
 Circular caitya with stupa and arch
 
 

 
 
B.

 
 Guntapalle
 
 
2.

 
 Pillared veranda with cells at the back
 
 

 
 
C.

 
 Khandagiri
 
 
3.

 
 Animal-shaped single rock excavations
solution:
The Correct answer is __**Option 4**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Udayagiri**: This site is renowned for its **Pillared veranda with cells at the back**. The caves here are mostly associated with Jain monks and are significant for their historical relevance in Indian architecture.
 
• **Guntapalle**: The architectural feature of this site includes the **Circular caitya with stupa and arch**. It is an important Buddhist site located in Andhra Pradesh and features unique structural characteristics.
 
• **Khandagiri**: It is famous for its **Animal-shaped single rock excavations**. The site, along with Udayagiri, is a prominent Jain monument in Odisha and displays intricate carvings and sculptures.
 
• The correct matching of the sites with their features ensures an accurate understanding of the architectural styles and their historical significance.
 
• The associations between the cave sites and their respective architectural features highlight the cultural and religious diversity in Indian cave architecture.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Udayagiri Cave Site**__

 __
 
• **Udayagiri** is located in the state of Odisha.
 
• The caves are an important Jain heritage site and include inscriptions related to Jain kings and monks.
 
• The site is believed to date back to the **2nd century BCE**.
 
• The caves feature simple yet functional designs with verandas and cells for ascetic living.
 
 
 
• **Guntapalle Cave Site**__
 __
 
• **Guntapalle** is located in Andhra Pradesh.
 
• It is a significant Buddhist site with architectural features such as a circular caitya and stupa.
 
• The site is known for its **rock-cut caves and monolithic stupas**.
 
• It provides insights into the development of Buddhist architecture in southern India.
 
 
 
• **Khandagiri Cave Site**__
 
 
• **Khandagiri**, along with Udayagiri, is located in Odisha.
 
• The caves are known for their **animal-shaped carvings** and rock-cut architecture.
 
• The site is associated with the **Jain religion** and displays inscriptions of King Kharavela.
 
• It features elaborate carvings, including depictions of animals, humans, and floral motifs.
